A curious spotted fawn watches from the ferns at the edge of the glade, unafraid.
A tiny carved door, no bigger than a book, is set into the mossy roots of an ancient tree.
A white stag stands motionless among the distant trees, antlers catching the moonlight like silver wire.
A sleeping hedgehog lies curled on a broad mushroom cap, perfectly still, softly breathing.
A ring of tiny dancing lights bobs slowly above the pool, tracing a patient circle.
A fox sits at the treeline, watching with amber eyes that hold far too much knowing.
A snail crosses a luminous leaf, leaving a faint silver trail that glows gently in the dark.
A tiny wooden boat, no longer than a hand, drifts slowly across the still moonlit pool.
A bird perches on a low branch, its feathers catching the light like scattered emeralds and sapphires.
A half-hidden stone face peers from the mossy bank, half-swallowed by roots and centuries of silence.
A trail of tiny pointed footprints crosses the soft mud and vanishes beneath a toadstool ring.
A single flower glows softly at the glade's edge, its petals lit from somewhere deep within.
A moth rests on a pale stone, its wings painted with two perfect golden eyespots.
Tiny silver fish drift just below the pool's surface, moving together as though sharing one thought.
A lantern no bigger than an acorn hangs from a thorn, casting warm amber light on nothing.
A spider's web between two reeds holds a single dewdrop that pulses faintly with pale blue light.
A cluster of mushrooms forms a perfect spiral staircase descending into the soft dark earth below.
An old tortoise moves through the undergrowth wearing a tiny sprig of white blossom on its shell.
A hummingbird hovers beside a night-blooming flower, wings invisible, eyes bright as polished jet.
Smooth river stones along the bank are each carved with a single small, unreadable rune.
A dragonfly perches on a reed, its wings casting tiny rainbows across the still water below.
A wren hops close and tilts its head, regarding you with an oddly patient, measuring intelligence.
Soft music drifts from somewhere beneath the roots, too faint to name, too clear to doubt.
A cloak of woven leaves hangs on a branch, abandoned, still warm as though just shrugged off.
A small glass bottle stopped with wax sits upright in the moss, holding one folded scrap of paper.
